RUBYOPT
Using this env variable itâs possible to
add new params
to
ruby
whenever it gets executed. Although the param
-e
cannot be used to specify ruby code to execute, itâs possible to use the params
-I
and
-r
to add a new folder to the libraries to load path and then
specify a library to load
.
Create the library
inject.rb
in
/tmp
:
puts `whoami`
Create anywahere a ruby script like:
puts 'Hello, World!'
Then make an arbitrary ruby script load it with:
RUBYOPT="-I/tmp -rinject" ruby hello.rb
Fun fact, it works even with param
--disable-rubyopt
:
RUBYOPT="-I/tmp -rinject" ruby hello.rb --disable-rubyopt
